Alright the overall goal of the project is to predict the cost of damage caused by any given tornado in the storm event data set. 



```{r}
library(knitr)
library(tinytex)
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = "60%",fig.align='center')
```

First lets load the data.

```{r}
storms_all <- read_csv("tornado_data.csv")
```

This includes a lot of predictor variables and has the damage listed in thousands, millions or billions of dollars. f_score is also not numerical when it should be so lets fix both of these

```{r}
 


storms_all2 <- storms_all %>%
  mutate(
    damage_clean = str_trim(tolower(damage)),                 # lowercase and trim spaces
    damage_value = parse_number(damage_clean),                # extract numbers
    damage_suffix = str_extract(damage_clean, "[kmb]$"),      # get k, m, or b at the end
    multiplier = case_when(
      damage_suffix == "k" ~ 1000,
      damage_suffix == "m" ~ 1000000,
      damage_suffix == "b" ~ 1000000000,
      TRUE ~ 1
    ),
    damage_num = damage_value * multiplier ,                  # convert all to pure numbers
      log_damage = log(damage_num + 1),
     f_score_num = as.numeric(str_extract(f_score, "\\d+")),
    state = factor(state),
    f_score_num = as.numeric(str_extract(f_score, "\\d+")),
    state = factor(state),
    month = factor(month),
    state = factor(state),
    county_name = factor(county_name),
    f_score = factor(f_score)

    
  )%>%
  na.omit()


```
This sets the damage value to a real number, the f_score to a real number and takes the log of the damage to bring the damage values closer together. Now I will split into training and testing and start making models. 


```{r}
set.seed(123)

train_index <- sample(1:nrow(storms_all2), 0.8 * nrow(storms_all2))

training <- storms_all2[train_index, ]
testing  <- storms_all2[-train_index, ]




null_model <- lm(log_damage ~ 1, data = training)

full_model <- lm(log_damage ~ tor_length + tor_width + injuries_deaths +
                   f_score_num + range + start_time + end_time + month + state,
                 data = training)
library(MASS)

step_model <- stepAIC(null_model,
                      scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model),
                      direction = "forward",
                      trace = TRUE)



```

Using forward stepwise looking at AIC as the error metric we see that the model using state, f_score, month, tornado width and length has the lowest AIC.
```{r}
summary(step_model)


```
R^2 of .375, now lets see the RMSE. Getting errors because some states are not in training set. 

```{r}
testing_clean <- testing %>%
  filter(state %in% step_model$xlevels$state) %>%
  droplevels()

#unique(testing$state)          # all states in test
#step_model$xlevels$state       # states used in model
#unique(testing_clean$state)    # should NOT include ALASKA now



test_pred_log <- predict(step_model, newdata = testing_clean)

test_pred <- exp(test_pred_log) - 1

test_rmse <- sqrt(mean((testing_clean$damage_num - test_pred)^2))
test_rmse


```


now to make plots for predictive results section: 

```{r}
# 1 diagnostic plot
# Figure 1: Residuals vs Fitted
plot(step_model, which = 1,
     main = "Figure 5: Residuals vs Fitted Plot for Final Log-Linear Model")




# 2 variable selection plot
# Figure 2: AIC Path During Forward Stepwise Selection
library(MASS)

step_path <- step_model$anova   # AIC trace
plot(step_path$AIC, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Step",
     ylab = "AIC",
     main = "Figure 6: AIC During Forward Stepwise Selection")



# Figure 3: Distribution of Prediction Errors
errors <- testing_clean$damage_num - test_pred

hist(errors,
     breaks = 40,
     main = "Figure 3: Distribution of Prediction Errors (Original Damage Scale)",
     xlab = "Error: Actual - Predicted Damage ($)")





library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data = testing_clean, aes(x = damage_num, y = test_pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 4: Predicted vs Actual Tornado Damage",
    x = "Actual Damage ($)",
    y = "Predicted Damage ($)"
  )


```

cross validated error: 

```{r}
library(boot)

# cross-validated error for the final model (with state)
loocv_final <- cv.glm(
  data   = training,     # IMPORTANT: same data used to fit step_model
  glmfit = step_model    # your final model with state
  # no K argument -> default is leave-one-out CV
)

# RMSE on the log scale
loocv_final_rmse_log <- sqrt(loocv_final$delta[1])
loocv_final_rmse_log



```

```{r}

model <- lm(log_damage ~ month + state + county_id + county_name +
tor_length + tor_width + injuries_deaths +
start_day + end_day + start_time + end_time + range +
f_score_num,data=storms_all2)
#execute forward stepwise
forward_model <- ols_step_forward_adj_r2(model)
#review selection steps
forward_model$metrics


best_forward_model <- lm(log_damage ~ county_name+f_score_num+state+month+tor_length+tor_width+range+injuries_deaths+start_time+end_time,data=storms_all2)
summary(best_forward_model)
anova(best_forward_model)


pred_log <- predict(best_forward_model, newdata = storms_all2)
pred_orig <- exp(pred_log) - 1

rmse_orig <- sqrt(mean((storms_all2$damage_num - pred_orig)^2))
rmse_orig



```

)




# --- Compute RMSE on the log scale for null vs final model ---

# Final model predictions on log scale
pred_log <- predict(best_forward_model, newdata = storms_all2)

model_rmse_log <- sqrt(mean((storms_all2$log_damage - pred_log)^2))

# Null model: always predict mean log_damage
null_pred_log <- mean(storms_all2$log_damage)
null_rmse_log <- sqrt(mean((storms_all2$log_damage - null_pred_log)^2))

# Put into a small data frame
rmse_df <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Null Model", "Final Log-Linear Model"),
  RMSE  = c(null_rmse_log, model_rmse_log)
)

# --- Figure 3: RMSE comparison plot ---

barplot(
  height = rmse_df$RMSE,
  names.arg = rmse_df$Model,
  main = "Figure 3: RMSE of Null vs Final Model (Log Scale)",
  ylab = "RMSE on log(damage + 1)",
  col = c("grey80", "skyblue"),
  ylim = c(0, max(rmse_df$RMSE) * 1.1)
)



# Turn off scientific notation
options(scipen = 999)

# Figure 4: Predicted vs Actual Damage
plot(
  storms_all2$damage_num,
  pred_orig,
  pch = 19,
  col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.3),
  xlab = "Actual Damage ($)",
  ylab = "Predicted Damage ($)",
  main = "Figure 4: Predicted vs Actual Tornado Damage"
)

# Add reference 45-degree line
abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

cross validation attempt again : nvm
```{r}


str(forward_model)






vars <- forward_model$metrics$variable

step_formulas <- lapply(seq_along(vars), function(i) {
  as.formula(
    paste("log_damage ~", paste(vars[1:i], collapse = " + "))
  )
})

rmse_vec <- c()

for (f in step_formulas) {
  m <- lm(f, data = storms_all2)
  pred_log <- predict(m, newdata = storms_all2)
  pred_orig <- exp(pred_log) - 1
  
  rmse <- sqrt(mean((storms_all2$damage_num - pred_orig)^2))
  rmse_vec <- c(rmse_vec, rmse)
}

plot(
  rmse_vec,
  type = "b",
  pch = 19,
  col = "firebrick",
  xlab = "Forward Step",
  ylab = "RMSE on Original Dollar Scale",
  main = "Figure 7: RMSE at Each Step of Forward Selection"
)

text(
  x = 1:length(rmse_vec),
  y = rmse_vec,
  labels = vars,
  pos = 3,
  cex = 0.7
)



plot(best_forward_model, which = 4, main = "Figure 8: Cook's Distance")

```
